newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks inch down in early trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks inch down in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks edged down in early Monday morning trade, in what looked like a near-term battle between bulls and bears following last week's historical events surrounding the death of Deng Xiaoping, brokers said.
"There are two camps out there market, with those short trying to depress the market, said Francis Wong, executive director at DBS Securities.
The Hang Seng Index was just 15 points down at 13,429 after 30 minutes of trade. Turnover was active at HK$1.32 billion traded.
Brokers said turnover, which is normally spreadly fairly evenly throughout the day in Hong Kong, been heavier than usual in the morning session.
After days of depressed, nervous trading, the index soared nearly 350 points on Thursday and Friday last week, following the announcement of the China's paramount leader death of Deng Xiaoping.
Brokers also said they expected more volatility in the index this week with the expiry of the February futures contract on Thursday.
The Hang Seng Index February contract was trading 25 points down at 13,400 with open interest still high at 34,353.
The property sector led the market down followed by utilities. The H share sector was the star performer, advancing 2.12 percent to 969.
Cheung Kong led the most active table, shedding HK$0.25 to HK$71.50 on turnover of HK$115.5 million. Sun Hung Kai Properties lost HK$1.00 to HK89.50.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings held steady at HK$189.00 while subsidiary Hang Seng Bank slipped HK$0.50 to HK$90.75. The banks report 1996 earnings on March 3.
Hong Kong and China Gas was unchanged at HK$14.60. The company reports its 1996 earnings on February 27.
Hongkong Telecom dropped HK$0.15 to HK$13.35 on thin volume of HK$31.46 million.

In the H share sector, Guandong Kelon was unchanged at HK$6.40. The share will report earnings for 1996 on Friday. Tsingtao Brewery put on HK$0.12 to HK2.975, and Dongfang Electrical added HK$0.15 to HK$2.50.
Red chip China Travel inched up HK$0.10 to HK$4.00.
Trade in China Merchants Hai Hong was active. The share advanced HK$0.25 to HK$4.625 on trade of HK$79.01 million. Analysts said more asset injections from the parent company are planned.
